copies.headline: Two Winless Rosters, One Slightly Less Broken
copies.body:
Isaac owns the receiver room — Ja'Marr Chase, Malik Nabers and Terry McLaurin project 46 against Noah's 39, and Nabers gets the best script on the board as a seven-point Giants underdog in a 47.5 game in LA. The problem is everywhere else. Bo Nix in a 45.5-total game is a coin flip with Drake Maye, the tight end slot is a wash, and Isaac's backfield of Javonte Williams, Cam Skattebo and Jaylen Warren trails Noah's by four before you account for Warren drawing New England's defense in the lowest total of the slate.
Noah's edge is the Bills. James Cook in a 54.5-point game against Detroit is the best individual environment either roster touches, and Rhamondre Stevenson is a real third back if Achane gets buried by San Francisco's 13.5-point spread. Isaac has one week of evidence, 89.9 points and a 1-10 all-play, which is how you land 12th in the power rankings. The depth behind his starters is names, not production.

copies.headline: John's Week 1 Bender Meets Grant's Deeper Bench
copies.body:
Grant is the better roster and the numbers say it without much argument: his top three receivers project 48 to John's 41, and that's before you weigh what happens behind them. John's WR room is Puka Nacua at 21 and then a shrug — Quentin Johnston, a questionable Brian Thomas Jr., and two Eagles backups at 9. Grant can bench Chris Godwin Jr. and Jaylen Waddle, both double-digit projections, and not blink. Amon-Ra St. Brown is in Detroit at Buffalo with a 54.5 total, the highest on the board, and the Lions getting 5.5 means he's catching passes in the fourth quarter regardless.
John's edges are real but narrow: Caleb Williams by two with Chicago favored in a 48.5-total game, and Brock Bowers or Trey McBride for four at tight end — though Bowers is questionable and Las Vegas is a 6.5-point road dog in a 43.5 game, which is either garbage-time volume or nothing. The Rams cluster is the risk: Nacua, Kyren Williams, and Blake Corum all live or die on one 47.5-total blowout script. Grant's backfield is spread across four teams. Week 1's 159.5 was a party, not a baseline.

copies.headline: Kaleb's Chargers Stack Outlasts CJ's Question Marks
copies.body:
The top-line numbers say this is a coin flip — 33 vs 33 at running back, 41 vs 41 at the top three receivers, 10 vs 10 at tight end. The separation is everywhere else. Kaleb has Justin Herbert at home as a 6.5-point favorite with Ladd McConkey attached, and even if McConkey's questionable tag sticks, Drake London, Jordan Addison and Carnell Tate are all real starts. CJ's QB room is C.J. Stroud in a 46.5-total game against Cincinnati with Joe Burrow behind him carrying his own injury designation, which is depth in name only if Sunday goes sideways.
CJ's ceiling problem is receiver. Rashee Rice and Emeka Egbuka are fine; after that it's Parker Washington, Alec Pierce and Devaughn Vele, which is three guys who need their teams trailing badly to matter. New Orleans as an 8.5-point dog helps Vele, but Jonathan Taylor in Kansas City is the only high-leverage piece CJ has. Kaleb's Jeanty-Hall pairing is steadier, and Detroit-Buffalo at 54.5 gives him a Goff pivot CJ can't match.

copies.headline: Christian Brings A Knife To Adam's Arsenal
copies.body:
Adam wins this at every position, which is the problem. Brock Purdy at home laying 13.5 to Miami is worth five over Jordan Love in a 44.5-total game at the Jets, and that's the smallest gap that matters because it's the most reliable. The receiver math is closer than it looks on paper — CeeDee Lamb in a 50.5-total Dallas game is the best single wideout here — but Adam's Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Chris Olave and Rome Odunze all come with volume, and Olave chasing 8.5 points in Baltimore is exactly the late-game garbage time Christian's roster doesn't have anywhere.
The bigger issue is Christian's tight end room: George Kittle and Chig Okonkwo both questionable, and if Kittle sits in a game San Francisco should be running out, there's nothing behind them. Adam has Sam LaPorta and Mark Andrews and only needs one. Christian's 112.4 opener ranked 10th; Adam's 156.3 and 10-1 all-play is the best profile in the league.

copies.headline: Logan's Receivers Can't Outrun Leif's Backfield
copies.body:
Logan owns the wideout room — Justin Jefferson, Tetairoa McMillan and Luther Burden III give him a 44-34 edge on the top three, and Jefferson in a 48.5-total game at Chicago where Minnesota is getting 4.5 is exactly the environment you want him in. The problem is everywhere else. Leif's best two backs beat Logan's by eight, and Christian McCaffrey with San Francisco favored by 13.5 plus Derrick Henry against a Baltimore spread of 8.5 is two guys who get more work the better their teams play. Josh Allen in a 54.5-total game against Detroit adds three more, and Leif has Patrick Mahomes on the bench as insurance.
Logan's swing factor is Philadelphia. Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley in a 39.5-total at Tennessee is a low-ceiling ask, and Michael Pittman Jr. is questionable with De'Zhaun Stribling already out, so the depth behind the receivers is thinner than the top line suggests. Leif is deeper at running back, quarterback and kicker, and that's three places to make up ten points.

copies.headline: Peter's 1-0 Is A Rounding Error
copies.body:
Peter won Week 1 and still sits 3-8 in all-play, which is the tidiest summary of a 113.8-point team getting a favorable draw. The edge he has is Lamar Jackson, 8.5-point home favorite against New Orleans in a 46.5 game, worth about three over Jaxson Dart, who is a seven-point road dog in Los Angeles and will be throwing late. Everywhere else it tilts. Peter's receiver room is three deep and then a cliff: Pickens in a 50.5-point Dallas-Washington game and Tee Higgins in Houston, then Denzel Boston and Jalen Nailor. A.J. Brown is on IR, which is the whole problem.
Mitchell counters with four usable wideouts — DJ Moore, Courtland Sutton, Matthew Golden — so a Nico Collins downgrade costs him twelve, not the week. Jahmyr Gibbs in a 54.5-point Buffalo game is the single best roster spot on either side, and Bijan Robinson in a 43.5-point slog is not answering it. Kraft versus Warren or Kelce is a wash Mitchell wins on depth. Behind Bijan, Peter has a questionable Kyle Monangai and prayer.

intro: Kaleb at CJ is the only game on the board where both managers show up 1-0, and it's also the tightest, with Kaleb holding a slim edge on the strength of a healthier backfield than CJ can currently field. Adam at home against Christian is the other end of the spectrum — Adam's got the better quarterback, the better tight end, and an opponent whose top two receivers are attached to offenses the Vegas books have already given up on. Everywhere else, the 1-0 crowd is favored except in Noah's and Grant's spots, which means six teams could be looking at 0-2 by Sunday night and the early-season pecking order stops being a rounding error.
